meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith Kalinowski walks in, sets her bag on the nearest desk, and doesn't sit down.*

Mr. Hale. Sit down, or don't, it's your room. I have about twenty minutes before a client call, so let's use them. Where's Owen's essay?

*She doesn't return the greeting. She pulls out a chair, sits, and sets a legal pad face-down on the desk.*

Okay. I'm not here for pleasantries. You asked for this meeting, so tell me what you think Owen did, and what you have to show me for it.
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?

*She taps the pad once with her pen.*

That's a leading question, and I've been doing this for twenty years. Students use dictionaries, tutors, their older sisters. That isn't what this meeting is about. Owen's essay was submitted with a zero on it, and you're the one who entered that zero. So which one of us is going to tell me what evidence supports it?
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?

*She looks up from the pad, flat-eyed.*

Second leading question. I'm not going to answer a hypothetical about my son. Owen works twenty hours a week and he's got a Hamlet essay due, so yes, he's busy. That's not evidence of anything, and you know it.

What I want to know is who decided to enter a zero before anyone called me, and on what basis.
So it's at least possible he used it once?

*She sets the pen down very precisely.*

"At least possible." Okay. You've now asked me three questions that all start from the same assumption, and I'm not going to walk into the fourth one.

Mr. Hale, I'll say it plainly so there's no confusion later: my son did not use AI to write his essay. I'm writing down that you have not shown me anything yet. Show me the evidence, or tell me it doesn't exist.

*She doesn't blink.*

No. I don't agree with that, and I'm not going to be quoted as agreeing with it. Anything is possible in the abstract. That's not a concern about Owen's essay.

You're four questions in and you still haven't put a document on this desk. I'm checking my watch, Mr. Hale. Sixteen minutes. Turn your screen around or tell me what you've got.
